payload.name: Preserve explicit reasons for actions and decisions
payload.description: When a message states a decision or action and explicitly gives reasons or motivations, include those reasons in the memory candidate so 'why' questions can be answered later.
content: When a message states a decision or action and explicitly gives reasons or motivations (e.g., 'because', 'felt like', 'was fascinated by'), include those reasons in the same memory candidate or as an additional memory, so the 'why' is preserved.

Before finalizing an extraction candidate, check whether the source sentence answers 'why did this happen?' If yes, the reason should appear in the memory content; do not replace it with only the event and its consequences.

solves: Extraction candidates often preserve the fact of an action or decision but drop the explicitly stated reasons or motivations, so later 'why' questions cannot be answered. This skill applies whenever a message contains an action/decision plus explicit reasons; the constructed memory must preserve both. It does not apply to reasons that are only implied or unsupported by the message.
